page: The Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a dedicated bare-metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe line. Powered by an Intel Xeon E-2388G processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz, it features 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads via hyper-threading. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is addressed via an integrated 3840 GB NVMe SSD array, while graphical processing units are absent. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capability, scoring 2184.0 on Geekbench single-core tests and demonstrating high throughput in compression routines such as single-threaded gzip (36.27 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.14 GB/sec). Multi-core operations position securely in the mid-tier, yielding 10124.0 points in Geekbench multi-core and 20287.03 in stress-ng multi-core testing. Small-model LLM generation (135M parameters) performs favorably at 275.61 tokens/sec, but medium models (7B parameters) achieve average rates around 9.95 tokens/sec.

Memory performance shows distinct operational tradeoffs. Cached operations and small block benchmarks score in top brackets, reflected in a PassMark memory score of 3390.33 and 1099.44 GB/sec for 16 KB read blocks. However, uncached large-block throughput drops notably, registering 36.93 GB/sec on large read blocks and 19.38 GB/sec on large write operations. The architecture includes hardware-level instruction sets such as AVX-512, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, which support cryptographic tasks and vectorized operations.

Given its combination of single-socket frequency, dedicated NVMe storage density, and 128 GB of memory, the server delivers high hardware-level isolation without virtualization overhead. It is best aligned with transactional databases, static web serving (measured at 12.59 GB/sec), in-memory caching systems such as Redis (processing 16.84 million SET operations per second), and CI/CD compilation workloads.
description: The Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a dedicated bare-metal instance powered by an 8-core, 16-thread Intel Xeon E-2388G processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. Supported by 128 GB of DDR4 memory and a fast 3840 GB NVMe SSD, the hardware lacks discrete GPUs but supplies dedicated non-virtualized resources with an included IPv4 address. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread efficiency, achieving high marks in Geekbench single-core tests (2184.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (36.27 GB/sec). Memory architecture performs well on localized, cached datasets as evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 3390.33, though uncached large-block bandwidth exhibits lower relative performance. With balanced processing power, dedicated NVMe capacity, and no hypervisor layer, the server is suitable for medium-scale database hosting, Redis key-value workloads, compilation pipelines, and static web serving.
